entries.title: Which Planet Has a Day Longer Than Its Year?
entries.description:
One planet finishes a year before it finishes one rotation: Venus.

One rotation day takes about 243 Earth days, while one orbit year takes only 225. On Venus, the slow retrograde rotation means the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

#Science #Venus #Space #Astronomy #Planets #VisualScience #SpaceFacts

entries.title: Which Planet Could Float in Water?
entries.description:
If a planet-sized ocean existed, one world would float: Saturn.

This gas giant has an average density of 0.68 grams per cubic centimetre, lower than liquid water. Although it has no solid surface, as a scale-impossible thought experiment, Saturn is light enough to float.

#Science #Saturn #Space #Astronomy #Planets #Ocean #Density #VisualScience

entries.title: Which Planet Has the Shortest Day?
entries.description:
Which planet spins through a full day in under ten hours? Jupiter.

It spins through a full rotation in just 9.9 hours. This extreme rotational speed generates huge centrifugal forces, flattening the poles and creating a distinct equatorial bulge.

#Science #Jupiter #Space #Astronomy #Planets #CentrifugalForce #ShortestDay #VisualScience

entries.title: Which Planet Has the Fastest Winds?
entries.description:
The solar system's fastest winds blow on the farthest major planet: Neptune.

Winds reach over 1,200 miles per hour, outrunning the speed of sound. Driven by internal heat flux rather than solar energy, these supersonic shear winds organize into giant dark vortex storms.

#Science #Neptune #Space #Astronomy #Planets #NeptuneWinds #GreatDarkSpot #VisualScience

entries.title: What If the Sun Disappeared Right Now?
entries.description:
What if the Sun vanished right now? For eight minutes, Earth would remain in light and orbit.

Gravity and light propagate at the exact same speed: the speed of light. Once the propagation delay passes, Earth would go dark and fly off in a straight tangent line into space.

#Science #Sun #Relativity #Gravity #LightSpeed #EarthOrbit #Space #Astronomy #VisualScience
